sentences.text: Now let’s put lights on a boat.
Rule twenty-three covers a power-driven vessel underway, and she shows a masthead light forward, sidelights, and a sternlight.
Here’s a vessel under fifty meters, coming straight at you.
You see one white masthead light, with red and green below it.
Red and green together means she’s head-on.
Now a vessel of fifty meters or more, showing you her starboard side.
She must carry a second masthead light, behind the first and higher.
A smaller vessel may carry one, but doesn’t have to.
Those two white lights work like a range.
The lower one is forward, so it points the way she’s heading.
And when the two lights start to close up or open out, she’s turning.
And here’s the option for boats under twelve meters: one all-round white light, plus sidelights.
That’s probably what’s on your center console right now.
So tonight at the dock, look at your own boat.
